category_title: Learners with ADHD in introductory programming
minimal_context: The student is watching a teacher demonstration on complex programming structures in Delphi and attempting to implement the code.
dialogue:
TUTOR: I am going to demonstrate a more complex programming structure in Delphi on my computer now. Watch my screen and try to follow along.

STUDENT: Okay, I have Delphi open on my screen and I'm watching yours.

TUTOR: I'm adding the new components and setting up the control properties. Go ahead and implement this.

STUDENT: Hold on, let me just type all these lines down exactly how you have them on your screen.

TUTOR: Can you explain how that programming structure works?

STUDENT: I don't really know what it does, I'm simply copying the code from your PC so mine looks the same.

options.A: Require that the student earns a minimum number of points during each Delphi programming class period (e.g., 1,000) when completing the assigned coding tasks.
options.B: Provide opportunities for the student to learn about software development occupations through community placements that match their specific needs and programming interests.
options.C: Chunk the programming material to an appropriate level and allow the student to implement the Delphi code as the demonstration progresses.
options.D: Create a congenial learning environment during demonstrations based on mutual trust, open communication, and a willingness to take risks without fear of negative consequences.
